title: Why startup biz dev deals fail: pitch big companies growth in the way they already make money
summary: Jason Cohen explains why startups' "win-win" distribution proposals get ignored by larger companies: a one-time revenue sliver is immaterial and costs the big company its reputation. Good biz dev brings the big company new customers in its existing business model, or generates material, repeating revenue (2%+ of top line).

principles.text: Startups lack distribution; big companies have it but struggle to innovate. That mismatch feels like a deal, but it isn't enough.
principles.quote: Distribution is the hardest thing for a young startup, defined as "getting in front of potential customers." Large companies, on the other hand, have solved the distribution problem

principles.text: A one-time revenue share from emailing a big company's customers is immaterial to them, so it never gets approved.
principles.quote: By definition a company earns 1% of their monthly revenue in about 8 hours. Increasing revenue, once, by 8 hours, isn't interesting.

principles.text: Pitching a partner's customer base costs them reputation that your equation ignores; asking them to market to customers is asking them to spam.
principles.quote: The amount of revenue in question is not interesting for the big company, yet it requires the big company to spend something not accounted for in the above equation: Reputation.

principles.text: Design the deal by asking how you can make the bigger company money in the way it already makes money.
principles.quote: How can the smaller company make money for the larger company *in the manner that the larger company already makes money?*

principles.text: Bring customers to the big company instead of milking its customers. Even a few recurring customers move the needle.
principles.quote: If you can bring customers to a big company--even a few--rather than milking their existing customers for a sliver of revenue, you're much more likely to execute a deal that genuinely makes both of you significant money.

principles.text: Alternatively, find a mechanism that repeatedly generates material revenue, which means 2% or more of the partner's top line.
principles.quote: "Material" is 2% or more of their top-line revenue, repeatedly.
